Conclusion: 智能体不仅写了代码，还写了大部分本应让人类掌控全局的规格；学生把自己的所有权安放在很少写下来的想法上，却很少能解释或修改代码，且其自述贡献与自己的提交记录互不相干；体量目标则被“毫无作用的代码”达成。成因不在于智能体制造了这些问题，而在于它把每一个问题都变得廉价。因此，采用智能体的课程应把评分对准智能体不提供的那部分：学生自己写的规格、所做的评审、能讲清楚的代码；并把工程流程从“信任学生或智能体”转为用工具强制执行。给教育者的具体建议：(1) 行数目标恰是智能体最擅长生产的量，应改用范围型目标，如验收标准被可证明满足的功能数量；(2) 明确决定规格由谁写——要求学生先以 Agent: none 提交初稿再让智能体修改并评估二者差异，或接受智能体起草而强制记录评审改了什么、为什么，并对少数验收标准做口头答辩；(3) 用 AGENTS.md 等指令让智能体自动加尾注、导出会话，CI 自动拒收缺规格或规格与代码同提的提交，使规模化评分可行；(4) 只写一次、从不修订的规格教不会实践，应在作业中途引入需求变更以迫使新规格明确替代关系；(5) 评估所有权而非仅产物：发布并能一键打开只证明智能体工作，不证明学生能解释、修改或答辩。有效性威胁包括：尾注归属仅为下界（未声明提交也可能来自智能体）、3 个项目无法计算规格先行、结构识别可能漏判小节、自陈所有权与粗粒度的 +manual 标记、22/109 份会话不可解析、学生知悉记录计入评分带来的社会赞许偏差、钻空子启发式会漏掉冗长但各异的填充（故为下界）、改写历史检测依赖 GitHub 活动记录、外部有效性限于单门选修课单校 18 组且工具演进极快，且 18 组样本的关联分析均为探索性。后续工作将在下一轮课程中要求学生自写规格初稿、按范围设目标、用 CI 强制约定，并跟踪同一批学生至学期项目与个人口头答辩，检验感知所有权能否预测其解释与修改代码的能力，并深入分析提示词——这一条智能体不代写的决策记录。

Abstract: Software engineering courses are starting to ask students to build entire systems with AI coding agents, but little is known about what students actually do with them and whether they still own what they deliver. If the agent writes both the code and the decisions behind it, the artifacts we grade no longer show what students learned. We studied an assignment in which 18 pairs of students built applications with agents under Spec-Driven Development, combining the mined history of their repositories, the prompts they recorded, and a survey of 33 students. The agents wrote 69\% of the specifications meant to keep students in control, sometimes from a prompt of a few words. Students locate their ownership in the ideas, crediting themselves with half of them but a fifth of the code, yet most could not explain that code to a colleague or modify it without the agent, and what they report having written is unrelated to what their own commits declare. The three teams that met the 100,000-line target did so with generated code the application never uses, in one case proposed by the agent itself, and one team rewrote its history to backdate its specifications. Teaching with agents should therefore assess what students specify, review, and can explain, rather than what they ship, and enforce the engineering process with tools rather than trusting it to students or agents.

</details>


### [675] [Beyond Leaderboard Ranks: Selecting Software Engineering Agents Under Budget Constraints](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21515)
*Srinath Srinivasan,Tim Menzies*

Main category: cs.SE

TL;DR: 本文用 Holistic Agent Leaderboard (HAL) 的 58,197 条 run–task 执行记录（聚焦 SWE-bench Verified Mini 及另外 6 个基准），把"选哪个 agent"从排行榜排名问题重新表述为"预算约束下的决策问题"。核心结论：排行榜排名证据薄弱——7 个基准中 35 个 accuracy–cost Pareto 前沿步长有 27 个统计上不可区分；SWE-bench 上 $34.16 的运行比 $170.78 的领先者仅低 14.6 个百分点却无法被统计区分；leaderboard 报告成本与标准化 token 成本差异最高达 11.7×；基于中等难度任务的采样会低估 20.4% 的全基准部署成本。在可预先查询单任务成本的设定下，successive halving 以穷尽评估开销的 6.6% 达到 Q=0.80 的不确定性感知选择目标，在 7 个基准中 6 个花费最低、1 个持平。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 软件团队引入 LLM agent 修复 issue 时面临两个预算：评估预算（试跑候选 agent 的开销）与部署预算（选定 agent 在真实 backlog 上的开销）。现有评测主要以 leaderboard 排名呈现，但排名本身不足以支撑付费决策：(1) 相邻排名之间的准确率差异可能在统计上不可分辨（小基准的分辨率下限高）；(2) 报告的成本口径不一致（缓存 token 重复计费、历史价目表），与标准化 token 成本可差一个数量级；(3) 评估候选 agent 本身代价高昂；(4) 为区分准确率而挑选的"中等难度"任务并非成本分布的代表性样本，据此推断的部署成本存在系统性低估。因此需要研究：在评估预算受限、部署成本有上限的条件下，如何高效选出既可负担又与最佳可负担候选者在统计上不可区分的 agent。

Method: 数据与成本重建：从 HAL 的 380 个公开 trace 归档中重建 58,197 条 run–task 记录（11 个基准，排除 4 个不完整者后保留 7 个），过滤后得到 262 个 run、20,633 个完整单元格；SWE-bench 保留 34 runs × 48 共享任务。成本按 C=(I−R−W)p_I + R·p_R + W·p_W + O·p_O 标准化 token 计费重建，模型统一到最新拟合价目期，缺失/非正成本用 run 内正成本中位数插补。统计：用配对精确 McNemar 检验 + BH 校正（q=0.05，共 5,371 次配对比较）判定"unresolved"；构建 accuracy–cost Pareto 前沿并统计前沿上不可分辨步长；给出分辨率下限 6/n 及 80% 检验功效的 MDE 模拟；用 bootstrap 区间、Bonferroni 校正做敏感性分析，并用 90% 区间是否落在 ±10pp 内区分"统计不拒绝"与"实际等效"。选择实验：把购买单元格 (i,j) 视为支付 C_ij 并揭示 Y_ij，穷尽成本 E=ΣC_ij，评估预算取 E 的 1%/2.5%/5%/10%/25%，部署上限 d 取真实全 run 成本分布的 25/50/100 分位；策略包括随机单元格、随机任务、round robin、最便宜优先、successive halving（SH，等额美元目标、每轮淘汰下半）、mid-range filtering（MR，10% 随机探测后优先 0.30–0.70 成功率任务）、行级 EZR（best-vs-rest 朴素贝叶斯 + EI 等变体）、单元格级 Distance-to-Heaven（D2H），对比"可预查成本"与"事后才知成本"两种信息边界；指标为不确定性感知选择分数 Q（在 U_d 内的比例）、all-caps 版本、真实可负担率、准确率 regret、exact-best，以及达到 Q=0.80 的插值最小花费（300 次重复，跨 10 个预算水平 200 次重复）。

Result: RQ1：7 个基准 35 个 Pareto 前沿步长中 27 个统计不可分辨（SWE-bench 4 步中 3 步）；34 runs×48 任务上 561 次配对中 40.1% 不可分辨；SWE-bench 上 $34.16 的候选落后 $170.78 领先者 14.6pp 但不可区分，5 倍成本溢价无证据支撑。原因在于分辨率下限 6/n（SWE-bench 12.5pp、AssistantBench 18.2pp 超过其 15.2pp 全距），模拟 MDE 达 20.7pp；不校正时仍有 21.0%–100% 配对不可分辨，但仅 4.8% 的 SWE-bench 配对 90% 区间落在 ±10pp 内，说明不拒绝≠等效。RQ2：333 个 run 的公布成本/重建成本比中位数 1.00、95 分位 5.00、最大 11.7×（两个 Anthropic run 缓存 token 被重复计数，一例 $1,789.67 vs $180.13；另有 16 个 o3 run 用旧 $10/$40 价目产生 5.0× 差异）；42 个 run 无可恢复 token 记录。采样偏差：oracle MR 在 SWE-bench/CORE-Bench 使估计成本/真实成本比降至 0.796/0.834（低估 20.4%/16.6%），随机任务采样为 0.985/0.933；最难任务（pass rate<0.30）单格均成本 $4.38，是中难度任务 $2.59 的 1.69×；加均匀成本探测可把比值拉回 1.006/1.037。RQ3：在可预查成本下 SH 在全部 7 个基准达到 Q=0.80（及 0.90），SWE-bench 上花 $353.62 即达穷尽成本 $5,399.89 的 6.55%，优于 D2H 的 $379.19 与 EZR 的 $942.20；在 6 个基准最低花费、1 个持平（CORE-Bench $744 vs 随机 $1,292；GAIA 上随机采样在 40% 内未达标）。25% 预算下 SH 选出真正可负担 run 的比例 91.2%–100%，regret 0.0–3.2pp，但 exact-best 仅 58.0%–99.7%（SWE-bench 60.5%）。无预查成本时 SH 优势收窄（4/7 领先），且每例都超预算（10% 预算下均超支，均值 $3.04，EZR 超支更大）；更复杂的启发式不稳定（EI 使 SWE-bench Q 降 0.132，95% CI [−0.169,−0.097]；D2H 加权变体在三个基准均下降）；早停以 λ=0.25 使 SWE-bench 预算少用 16.1pp 但 Q 从 0.756 降到 0.614。

Conclusion: 论文主张 agent 评测应从"复现排行榜"转向"支撑决策"：(1) leaderboard 应同时报告准确率不确定性与执行成本，并说明哪些排名差异在统计上无证据支撑；(2) 评估预算与部署成本应分开报告，保留任务级 token 用量、缓存计费与价目表以便复现，标准化价目表可消除历史定价带来的虚假差异；(3) 成本估计需独立于准确率采样，用独立的均匀成本探测校准，因为难任务更贵也更易失败，按难度过滤的采样会系统性低估部署开销；(4) 应把 successive halving 这类简单自适应分配作为基线，任何更复杂的采集/早停启发式必须相对它有一致改进才值得采用；(5) 应在团队真实 issue backlog 上以补丁审查为结果指标做前瞻性验证。局限包括：成本仅含 API token 支出、不含托管/外部工具/人工审查；仅 4 组重复配置可评估执行随机性；配对检验忽略同仓库 issue 间的相关性且 BH 在任意依赖下不保证 FDR 控制；重放基于历史固定结果而非新鲜执行；Q 指标在低分辨率基准上会偏袒策略，需结合 all-caps、可负担率、regret、exact-best 解读。

Abstract: Teams that adopt LLM agents for issue resolution must decide which agent to pay for, and how much to spend finding out. Leaderboard ranks give weak evidence for this decision. Accuracy differences may be statistically unresolved, reported costs may be inconsistent, and evaluating candidate agents can itself be expensive. We investigate budget-constrained agent selection using 58,197 run--task records extracted from the Holistic Agent Leaderboard (HAL), focusing on SWE-bench and six additional benchmarks. Across seven benchmarks, 27 of 35 steps along the accuracy--cost Pareto frontiers are statistically unresolved. On SWE-bench, a run costing $34.16 trails the $170.78 leader by 14.6 percentage points, but the available tasks cannot statistically distinguish their accuracy. Reported costs also differ from standardized token-based estimates by up to 11.7x, while selective task evaluation can bias estimates of full-benchmark execution cost. We therefore compare evaluation strategies under explicit evaluation budgets and deployment-cost caps. Under advance knowledge of task costs, successive halving reaches our uncertainty-aware selection target on SWE-bench using 6.6% of exhaustive evaluation spend, achieving the lowest cost on six of seven benchmarks and tying on the seventh. Its advantage narrows when task costs are unknown before execution or exact-best selection is required. Our findings motivate decision-oriented agent evaluation that accounts for accuracy uncertainty, validates execution costs, and compares complex selection methods against simple adaptive allocation.

</details>

### [676] [Tight Bounds for Non-Monotone Submodular Maximization under a Cardinality Constraint with Constant Recourse](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20257)
*Vaneet Aggarwal*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: 针对"元素逐个到达、每次到达后必须报告一个基数受限的非单调（non-monotone）次模集合，且每次到达对报告集的改动（recourse）有常数上界"这一流式场景，本文给出并证明了紧确界：常数 recourse 下可达到的最优极限逼近比为 1/4。具体地，存在算法在每个时刻以期望值保证 (1/4−ε)·OPT_t，recourse 为 O(ε^{-2})，且仅对已到达元素做多项式次数的值查询；同时证明即使拥有完全前瞻、无限计算与任意查询，任何常数 recourse 算法的比率也不超过 1/4，且任何固定超过 1/4 的比率都需要随基数预算 k 以某个正幂次增长的 recourse。此前常数 recourse 下的最好比率为 3−2√2≈0.172，故 1/4 相对提升约 45.7%。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 在实际流式应用中（用户摘要、训练子集、缓存集合），所选集合必须在每次新元素到达后即刻可用，而替换已选元素有成本，因此需要限制"每次到达的插入/删除次数"（recourse），而非仅限制总改动量。次模函数带来收益递减，但非单调性（如加权有向图的割函数）意味着加入新元素可能降低已有集合的价值，算法必须同时插入与删除。对于单调目标，Fu et al. (2026) 已证明常数 recourse 下最优比率为 2−√2，但该分析无法迁移到非单调情形；同时把离线最优解 (≈0.4634, Aggarwal & Du 2026) 在每个前缀上重跑虽保留比率，却会让相邻两次输出相差至多 2k 个元素（recourse 过大），而离线可证上界仅 0.4704。因此需要在"比率—recourse"权衡中精确刻画非单调次模最大化在基数约束、常数 recourse 下的最优极限比率。

Method: 下界（可达成）部分（第4节）：模型为元素按序到达、每次报告 |S_t|≤k 的可行集，recourse 定义为 |S_t △ S_{t−1}|，只允许对已到达集合做值查询。核心机制是"分数解 + 检查点 + 渐进替换"：①维护一个半整数分数解 y∈[0,1/2]^V（每元素被选概率≤1/2）；②在随机检查点（每个长度为 b=Lw 的块内随机选取位置 s_j=jb+U_j w）用 Algorithm 2 在截断多面体 P_K(X)={x∈[0,1/2]^X: Σx_e≤K} 上求近似稳定点——用采样估计 F 的偏导，取 2K 个最大正估计构成 z，取对偶变量 λ（(2K+1)大坐标），通过加/删/交换的半整数步改进，使对偶间隙 Γ_K(x,λ)=U_K(g,λ)−⟨x,g⟩≤ηM；③关键不等式（Lemma 4）：D_K(x;λ)=Kλ+Σ_e[(1−x_e)(∂_eF(x))_+−λ]_+ ≤ F(x)+2Γ 且 Kλ≤F(x)+Γ；新元素若估计边际 ĝ>ξ 则置 y_e=1/2，使 F 增量 g/2 恰好覆盖 D 中新增项 [g/2−λ]_+，因此不等式在后续到达中持续成立（Lemma 6：F(y_t) ≥ K/(2(k+K))·OPT_t − Γ_s − (2K/(k+K))Σξ）；④报告集用随机 pipage rounding 的"核" O_s（Lemma 2：允许事后加入元素仍保持 E f(O∪Z) ≥ F(x+z)）加上按 1/2 概率标记的后续到达元素构成候选解 C_t；⑤通过队列先删后插、每次到达执行 r=⌈2k/w⌉≤8L² 步，在长度 w 的窗口内完成从旧核到新核的替换，保证 |S_t|≤k 且每次到达改动 ≤ r+1 ≤ 8L²+1 = O(ε^{-2})。k<4L² 时退化为带 2k 虚拟哑元的 Random Greedy（比率 1/e>1/4）。上界部分（第5节）：构造加权有向图割函数实例，元素分成 m 组，组大小 d_i=q^{m−i}（几何递减）依次到达，组 i→组 j (j<i) 的弧权重为 W_i/((i−1)d_i d_j)，W_i=ρ^{i−2}，故 f(G_i)=W_i 而 OPT_{t_i}≥W_i。常数 recourse 意味着旧组被选比例几乎固定（|θ_{j,i}−θ_j| ≤ C/(q−1)），新组权重按 ρ 增长故完成时主导价值；用 φ_i=1−(1/(i−1))Σ_{j<i}θ_j 得递推 φ_{i+1}=φ_i+c_i/i，平方后望远镜求和给出 2Σ(θ_iφ_i−1/4)/i ≤ H_m^{(2)}，期望后即得 α ≤ 1/4 + C/(q−1) + 1/(ρ−1) + H_m^{(2)}/(2(H_m−1))，令 q,ρ→∞、m→∞ 得 α≤1/4；同一构造给出 Corollary 11：欲超过 1/4 需 C_k ≥ (β/2)(⌊k^{c_β}⌋−1)，即 k^{o(1)} 的 recourse 不足以超过 1/4。

Result: 定理3（可达成）：对任意 ε>0，存在算法对每个时刻 t 满足 E f(S_t) ≥ (1/4−ε)·OPT_t，recourse 为 O(ε^{-2})（具体 ≤ 8L²+1，L=max{2,⌈1/ε⌉}），查询次数至时间 N 为 O(N⁸ε^{−3}log((N+1)/ε))，全部查询仅作用于已到达元素的子集，且不使用流长度。定理10（上界）：在完全前瞻 + 无限查询/计算的模型下，任何 recourse ≤ C 的算法有 α ≤ 1/4 + C/(q−1) + 1/(ρ−1) + H_m^{(2)}/(2(H_m−1))，故常数 recourse 时 α ≤ 1/4。推论11：达到 1/4+β 需要 C_k ≥ (β/2)(⌊k^{c_β}⌋−1)，c_β=1/(m_β−1)，m_β=⌈exp(1+π²/(3β))⌉。综合表：无 recourse 限制时可达 0.4634…−ε、上界 0.4704…；常数 recourse 下可达 1/4−ε、上界 1/4。1/4 比 3−2√2≈0.172 高出约 45.7%，代价是 recourse 常数随 ε 减小而增大。

Conclusion: 常数 recourse 下，非单调次模最大化在基数约束下的最优极限比率为 1/4，且该结论在"仅对已到达元素做多项式查询"的受限模型与"完全前瞻 + 无限查询"的宽松模型之间同时成立，因而 1/4 是所有中间模型的极限阈值；任何固定高于 1/4 的比率都必须让 recourse 以 k 的某个正幂次增长，k^{o(1)} 的 recourse 不够。方法论要点是：半整数分数解（选概率≤1/2）配合近似稳定性不等式使得"每可行集价值 ≤ 常数×随机集期望值"的界在后续到达中保持成立，从而在最优值暴涨时仍稳健；渐进替换（先删后插 + 预留预算）保证可行性并把每步改动限制在常数。遗留开放问题：(i) 达到 1/4−ε 所需的最小 recourse 关于 ε 的最佳依赖；(ii) 所需的最小查询次数。

Abstract: We study the maximization of a nonnegative submodular function under a cardinality constraint when elements arrive one at a time and an algorithm must report a feasible set after every arrival. The recourse of an algorithm is the largest number of insertions and deletions that it makes to the reported set at a single arrival. For every $\epsilon>0$, we give an algorithm with recourse $O(\epsilon^{-2})$ whose reported set has, at every time, expected value at least $1/4-\epsilon$ times the largest value of a feasible set of arrived elements. The algorithm evaluates the function polynomially often, and only on sets of arrived elements. We also show that no algorithm with constant recourse achieves a ratio above $1/4$, even if it knows the function and the arrival order in advance and has unlimited computation, and that any fixed ratio above $1/4$ requires recourse that grows as a positive power of the cardinality budget. Thus $1/4$ is the optimal limiting ratio with constant recourse. The previous best ratio with constant recourse was $3-2\sqrt2\approx0.172$. Our algorithm assigns selection probabilities of at most one half and maintains, as elements arrive, an inequality bounding the value of every feasible set by a multiple of the expected value of a random set drawn with these probabilities; the reported set moves to a rounding of these probabilities through gradual replacements. The upper bound uses a weighted directed graph whose vertices arrive in groups of decreasing sizes.

</details>


### [677] [A PTAS for Euclidean Capacitated Vehicle Routing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19018)
*Zachary Friggstad,Fabrizio Grandoni,Ramin Mousavi,Kinter Ren,Mohammad R. Salavatipour*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: In the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP), introduced by Dantzig and Ramser in 1959, we are given an $n$-node graph $G=(V,E)$ with metric edges costs $c(e)$, a depot $r\in V$, and an integer vehicle capacity $Q$. The goal is to find a minimum-cost collection of tours, each containing the depot and visiting at most other $Q$ nodes, such that the tours cover all the nodes. In this paper we focus on the Euclidean CVRP problem, where the nodes represent points on $\mathbb{R}^2$, and the edge costs are the respective Euclidean distances. Euclidean CVRP generalizes the classical NP-hard Euclidean TSP problem (the special case with $Q=n-1$), that admits a PTAS [Arora FOCS'96/Mitchell SODA'96]. A long-standing open problem has been generalizing the latter PTAS to Euclidean CVRP. A polynomial-time $(2+\epsilon)$-approximation for this problem follows from the PTAS for Euclidean TSP and the tour-partitioning technique for CVRP [Haimovich, Kan Math. OR'85]. This was the best known until a recent improvement of the approximation factor to slightly below 2 [Friggstad, Grandoni, Mousavi SODA'26]. There have been a series of papers presenting improved QPTASs by Das and Mathieu [SODA'10] (time $n^{\log^{O(1/\epsilon)}n}$), Jayaprakash and Salavatipour [SODA'22] (time $n^{O_{\epsilon}(\log^6 n)}$), and recently Sitters [ArXiV'25] (time $n^{O_{\epsilon}(\log\log n)}$). In this paper, we solve the mentioned long-standing open problem by presenting a PTAS for Euclidean CVRP.

### [678] [Matroid Parity Meets Vertex Splitting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19278)
*Hitendra Kumar,Pritesh Kumar,Madhumita Kundu,Saket Saurabh*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: A vertex split replaces a vertex by two non-adjacent descendants and partitions its incident edges between them. We study exclusive $\ell$-shallow splitting, where each original vertex has at most $\ell+1$ descendants, with the aim of obtaining a forest, a pseudoforest, or a cluster graph. We consider two natural objectives: minimizing the total number of split operations and minimizing the number of original vertices that are split. Our main conceptual contribution is a connection between vertex splitting and matroid parity. For both forests and pseudoforests, we give a characterization of feasible splitting sequences that leads, via weighted linear matroid parity, to polynomial-time algorithms for minimizing the number of split vertices when $\ell=2$. These algorithms are complemented by NP-hardness for every fixed $\ell\ge3$; for pseudoforests, hardness holds even on graphs of maximum degree four. The total number of split operations behaves differently: for both sparse target classes, this objective is polynomial-time solvable for every $\ell$, using matroid intersection. For cluster graphs, both objectives admit linear-time algorithms when $\ell=1$ and are NP-hard for every fixed $\ell\ge2$. Together, these results identify how the target class, the local splitting bound, and the choice of objective determine the complexity of vertex splitting.

### [679] [Important Cuts with Logical Constraints: A Meta-Theorem for Eulerian Digraphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19368)
*Václav Blažej,Satyabrata Jana,Jędrzej Olkowski,M. S. Ramanujan,Peter Strulo*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Important separators are a standard tool in parameterized cut algorithms. An $S$-$T$ separator is important if it is inclusion-wise minimal and no separator of at most the same size leaves a strict superset of the vertices reachable from $S$ after deletion. Their use relies on a boundedness theorem: for fixed $k$, the number of important $S$-$T$ separators of size at most $k$ is at most a constant ($4^k$ to be precise) independent of the input size, even in directed graphs, and they can be enumerated efficiently. The classical theory, however, controls only the size of the separator, not the structure of the source side cut off by it. Once the source side is required to satisfy a condition such as acyclicity, bipartiteness, or another logical property, the corresponding maximal source sides can be unbounded in general digraphs. This obstruction is fundamentally related to hardness phenomena in directed deletion problems such as Directed Odd Cycle Transversal}. Prior to this work, even in undirected graphs, boundedness of such maximal constrained source sides was known only in more specialized settings, not at the level of generality considered in our work.

### [680] [Cogirth-Strength Ratios and Matroid Rank Reduction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19447)
*Yu Cong,Chao Xu,Yajie Zhao*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: In the rank-$p$ reduction problem, we are given a matroid with nonnegative element weights and seek a minimum-weight set of elements whose deletion lowers the rank by at least $p$. For graphic matroids, this is the minimum $(p+1)$-cut problem. Chekuri, Quanrud, and Xu developed a tree-packing algorithm for minimum $k$-cut, which relies on the fact that the minimum cut of a graph is at most twice its strength, the value of a maximum fractional packing of spanning trees. We generalize this approach from graphs to matroids. The matroid analogue of the minimum cut is the cogirth, the minimum weight of a cocircuit, and the analogue of graph strength is matroid strength, the value of a maximum fractional packing of bases. We show that if every matroid in a deletion-closed class has cogirth at most $d$ times its strength, then for every $p$, the natural linear programming relaxation of rank-$p$ reduction is within a factor of $d$ of the optimum. As a result, repeatedly deleting a minimum-weight cocircuit gives a $d$-approximation, and an optimal solution can be found deterministically in $n^{(2d-1)p+O(1)}$ time on $n$ elements. For graphs, $d=2$ and our framework specializes to the tree-packing approach. As applications, we bound the cogirth-strength ratio for two broad classes, and both bounds are tight. For quasi-graphic matroids, which include graphic, bicircular, frame, and lifted-graphic matroids, the ratio is at most $2$ for all weights, giving a $2$-approximation and an exact $n^{3p+O(1)}$-time algorithm. For $(k,\ell)$-count matroids of hypergraphs with $0\le \ell\le k$ and edge size at most $s$, the ratio is at most $ks$ under unit weights. This gives a $ks$-approximation and an exact $n^{(2ks-1)p+O(1)}$-time algorithm for unweighted rank-$p$ reduction.

### [681] [Tight Bounds for Differentially Private Cut Release](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19538)
*Chenghua Liu,Boning Meng*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for releasing a nonnegative weighted synthetic graph under $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-edge differential privacy. Given an $n$-vertex nonnegative weighted graph $G=(V,w_G)$, the output $H=(V,w_H)$ satisfies, with probability at least $1-\beta$, simultaneously for every $S\subseteq V$, $|w_G(S,V\setminus S)-w_H(S,V\setminus S)| \le\gamma w_G(S,V\setminus S)+O\bigl((n\log n)/(\varepsilon\gamma)\bigr)$, provided that $\gamma,\varepsilon,\delta,\beta$ are at least inverse polynomial in $n$. For constant $\gamma,\varepsilon$ and $\delta=\beta=n^{-10}$, this improves the recently obtained additive error bound of $O(n\log^7 n)$ to $O(n\log n)$. We also prove a matching $\Omega(n\log n)$ lower bound. Our algorithm combines degree decomposition with private multiplicative weights, using a degree-sensitive semidefinite oracle to generate update proposals from single Gaussian samples. Each proposal is validated by a noisy check of its exact entropy decrease, and a joint Rényi analysis of sampling and validation avoids additional logarithmic losses.

### [682] [Optimal mixing of random-to-random shuffling on linear extensions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19829)
*Haoran Wang*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Uniform sampling of linear extensions is a basic problem in randomized algorithms and the study of finite posets. We prove that the random-to-random shuffle of Ayyer, Schilling, and Thiéry mixes in $O(n\log n+n\log(1/\varepsilon))$ steps on every $n$-element poset, establishing their conjectured mixing order. With constant-time order queries, this gives an $\varepsilon$-approximate uniform sampler using $O(n^2(\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon)))$ elementary operations after preprocessing. The proof establishes relative-entropy contraction by a factor $1-1/n$ for the promotion half-step. Consequently, the uniform extended-promotion chain has the same mixing order. We represent complete promotion scans as reflected coordinate paths in the order polytope and prove that a convex potential with gradients in the same polytope has diagonal Hessian mass at most one along each path. Applying this estimate to an optimal transport potential yields a sharp entropy factorization for every finite-entropy input. Linearization also gives the spectral-gap lower bound $(n+1)/n^2$.

### [683] [IsaGraphLib: Formally Verified Efficient Graph Algorithms in Isabelle/HOL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20039)
*Mohammad Abdulaziz,Thomas Ammer,Adem Rimpapa,Peter Lammich*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We present a library of formally verified graph algorithms in Isabelle/HOL. The library covers the main problems of combinatorial optimisation on graphs: reachability, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees, matching, maximum flow, and minimum-cost flow. The algorithms in the library use most of the standard algorithm design techniques: graph search, greedy algorithms on matroids, dynamic programming, augmenting paths, blossom contraction, blocking flows, push-relabel, scaling, the primal-dual method, randomisation, and certificate checking. The library has adaptors between different types of graphs (directed, undirected, multigraphs), which allow results to be reused. Each algorithm is verified independently of its data structures, and the main algorithms are refined to efficient imperative implementations, from which we generate code in Standard ML, Scala, and Go. We developed parts of the library with large language models (LLMs), improved the quality of their proofs with a method based on statistics of our own proofs, and labelled which parts were developed by humans, by LLMs, or collaboratively. We perform a detailed experimental analysis of representative algorithms in our library, comparing it with state-of-the-art mainstream libraries, showing that our implementations are practical.

### [684] [Optimal Pattern-Avoidance Bounds for Binary Search Trees](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20088)
*Anita Dürr,Arturo Merino,Karol Węgrzycki,Sorrachai Yingchareonthawornchai*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Self-adjusting binary search trees (BSTs) perform better than balanced BSTs if the access sequence has additional structure. For example, splay trees serve a sequential access sequence in linear time. Pattern avoidance captures regularity in an access sequence and unifies several classic examples of efficient BST access, such as deque and traversal sequences. A central question is how well a BST algorithm can exploit a pattern-avoiding access sequence. We present an online BST algorithm that serves an access sequence avoiding a permutation pattern $\pi$ in linear time, matching the information-theoretic lower bound. The algorithm does not need to know that pattern $\pi$ a priori. Our results answer an open problem asked by [Kozma 2016, Problem 44, strong variant]. Previously, the best known offline bound was optimal only for constant-size patterns [Berendsohn, Kozma, and Opler, STOC'24], and the best known online bound was superlinear [Chalermsook, Pettie, Yingchareonthawornchai, SODA'24] even for a constant-size pattern. As a corollary, our BST algorithm yields an optimal sorting algorithm for a pattern-avoiding sequence that supports online insertions. Previously, an optimal sorting algorithm was achieved using a mergesort-like approach [Opler, FOCS'24] in a batch setting. A key technique is to apply recursive split decomposition [Chalermsook, Chuzhoy, Saranurak, ToC'23] jointly in time and space, along with the Marcus-Tardos proof of the Stanley-Wilf conjecture. We show that the framework can be implemented online using $k$-finger BSTs, which is of independent interest. Finally, this framework also yields a constant-factor-approximation FPT algorithm in the offline setting.

### [685] [Multi-seed information diffusion with varying reproduction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20284)
*Erin Meger,Arianne Nantel,Nicholas Saloufakos,Jessica Enright*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We define the $S_hR_k$-process that generalizes the notion of Hamiltonicity through the lense of information diffusion. We say that a graph is $S_hR_k$-infectable if it can be fully infected by transmission trees seeded by at most $h$ initial infections in which each infection leads to at most $k$ others; or, equivalently, if it can be exactly vertex-covered by at most $h$ trees of degree at most $k$. While determining $S_hR_k$ infectability is NP-hard in general, we argue fixed-parameter tractability when parameterised by treewidth. Additionally, we give computational experimental results comparing the performance of several natural heuristics for minimising the number of initial infections required to an optimal LP-based approach on several standard complex network models. We find that a uniformly random approach outperforms greedy heuristics based on degree or clustering.

### [686] [Minimum Sum-of-Radii Clustering with Strong and Weak Oracles](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20359)
*Zachary Friggstad,Mahya Jamshidian,Ali Vakilian*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: In the minimum sum of radii (MSR) problem, the input is a set of $n$ points in a metric space and a parameter $k$, and the goal is to cover the points by at most $k$ balls, each centered at an input point, while minimizing the sum of their radii. We study MSR in the weak-strong oracle model of Bateni, Dharangutte, Jayaram, and Wang (COLT'24), where the metric is unknown and is accessed through two oracles. The answers of the weak oracle are given to us for free: for every pair of points, we receive a distance value that, with probability $\delta$, is arbitrarily corrupted. Exact distances are available only through costly strong queries, where a strong query on a point reveals its exact distances to all previously strongly queried points, and the goal is to minimize the number of strong queries. For every constant $\delta < 1/2$, we give the first polynomial-time algorithm that makes $O(k \log n \log\log n)$ strong point queries and, with high probability, returns an $O(1)$-approximation for MSR; the previously best algorithm required running time and a number of strong queries exponential in $k$. This is within an $O(\log\log n)$ factor of a lower bound that we prove: any constant-factor approximation that succeeds with high probability on every instance must make $\Omega(k \log n)$ strong queries in expectation on some instance. The same $\Omega(k \log n)$ lower bound holds for $k$-center, where it matches the known upper bound up to an $O(\log\log n)$ factor. An optimal MSR cluster can be small both in size and in radius, so a uniform sample of strongly queried points may miss it entirely. Instead, our algorithm uses a packing LP over the balls certified so far to decide which points to query next. The analysis holds against an adversary who knows which pairs are corrupted.

### [687] [Online and Fully-Dynamic Sorting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20473)
*Yossi Azar,Sujoy Bhore,Devdan Dey,Debmalya Panigrahi,Or Vardi,Ian Zhang*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Online sorting asks how to place $n$ sequentially arriving elements in an array to minimize the sum of absolute differences between consecutive elements. Fully-dynamic sorting further extends the problem to allow both element insertions and deletions. Without recourse, these problems face strong lower bounds on the competitive ratio: $\Omega(\sqrt{n})$ for online sorting and $\Omega(n)$ for fully-dynamic sorting. In sharp contrast, we show that allowing only poly-logarithmic recourse yields at least exponential improvements in the competitive ratio for both problems:(1) Our main algorithmic result is a deterministic fully-dynamic sorting algorithm that is $O(\log^2 n)$-competitive and has $O(\log^4 n)$ amortized recourse per update. We complement this with a lower bound showing that any deterministic algorithm with any $O(\mathrm{polylog}(n))$ competitive ratio has amortized recourse at least $\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})$.(2) For the insertion-only setting, we establish a family of approximation--recourse tradeoffs, including $O(\log\log n)$ competitive ratio with $O(\log\log n)$ amortized recourse. Given the lower bound in the fully-dynamic case, this result shows that the insertion-only problem yields exponentially better bounds than the fully-dynamic one.(3) Finally, we show that the stronger approximation-recourse tradeoff for the insertion-only case extends to the fully-dynamic setting when the array has $(1+\varepsilon)n$ space.

### [688] [Rounded Potentials Certify Exact Maximum Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20475)
*Ohad Trabelsi*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: The textbook certificate for maximum flow is lopsided: the cut takes one bit per vertex, while the flow takes one number per edge. Indeed, some graphs have $\Theta(n^2)$ terminal pairs for which every maximum flow uses $\Theta(n^2)$ edges. Yet we show that one short number per vertex suffices for both cut and flow: $n$ vertex potentials, each rounded to $O(\log(nW))$ bits, certify the exact maximum $st$-flow value in any directed graph with integer capacities at most $W$. Exact potentials can have exponentially large representations. Rounding them may violate flow conservation, but the total error across any cut is less than one unit, so integrality of cut capacities absorbs it. Checking conservation is local and linear in the capacities, allowing the same certificate to yield new bounds in four models (capacities are polynomially bounded unless stated otherwise): - Online annotated streaming. $\widetilde{O}(n)$ total cost (help plus space) for the maximum $st$-flow value, optimal up to logarithmic factors, answering a question of Thaler (ICALP 2016) on whether $o(n^2)$ is possible. - Broadcast proof-labeling. $O(\log(n+p))$-bit labels certifying a maximum $st$-flow value of $p$ in directed and undirected graphs with arbitrary capacities, optimal for $p\ge n^{\Omega(1)}$, settling that regime of a question of Korman, Kutten, and Peleg (Distributed Computing 2010). - Merlin-Arthur verification. $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ time and $O(n^3\log n)$ proof length for directed All-Pairs Max-Flow, improving on previous verification times of $n^{4+o(1)}$ for general capacities and $n^{3.5+o(1)}$ for unit capacities, and answering a question of Akmal (TheoretiCS 2024). - Nondeterministic algorithms. $O(n^{3.614})$ time for directed All-Pairs Max-Flow, or $n^{3.5+o(1)}$ if $\omega=2$: the first subquartic bound for general edge capacities, answering a question of Trabelsi (SODA 2025).

Checking conservation is local and linear in the capacities, allowing the same certificate to yield new bounds in four models (capacities are polynomially bounded unless stated otherwise): - Online annotated streaming. $\widetilde{O}(n)$ total cost (help plus space) for the maximum $st$-flow value, optimal up to logarithmic factors, answering a question of Thaler (ICALP 2016) on whether $o(n^2)$ is possible. - Broadcast proof-labeling. $O(\log(n+p))$-bit labels certifying a maximum $st$-flow value of $p$ in directed and undirected graphs with arbitrary capacities, optimal for $p\ge n^{\Omega(1)}$, settling that regime of a question of Korman, Kutten, and Peleg (Distributed Computing 2010). - Merlin-Arthur verification. $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ time and $O(n^3\log n)$ proof length for directed All-Pairs Max-Flow, improving on previous verification times of $n^{4+o(1)}$ for general capacities and $n^{3.5+o(1)}$ for unit capacities, and answering a question of Akmal (TheoretiCS 2024). - Nondeterministic algorithms. $O(n^{3.614})$ time for directed All-Pairs Max-Flow, or $n^{3.5+o(1)}$ if $\omega=2$: the first subquartic bound for general edge capacities, answering a question of Trabelsi (SODA 2025).

</details>


### [689] [When is Uniform Sampling Optimal? Coresets for Distributional Clustering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20641)
*Junqiu Hu,Lingxiao Huang,Baoduo Xu*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Recent work [1] settled the optimal worst-case strong $\varepsilon$-coreset size for Euclidean $k$-means in unrestricted dimension at $\tilde{\Theta}(\min\{k^{3/2}\varepsilon^{-2}, k\varepsilon^{-4}\})$, showing that the natural target $\tilde{O}(k\varepsilon^{-2})$ is unattainable in general. For mixtures of $k$ isotropic Gaussian components with balanced weights and bounded scale imbalance in dimension $d\ge\log k$, we show that uniform sampling yields strong $\varepsilon$-coresets of size $\tilde{O}(k\varepsilon^{-2})$, without cluster separation. This saves a factor of $\min\{\sqrt{k},\varepsilon^{-2}\}$ over the worst-case bound, up to logarithms. For population approximation by independent, equally weighted samples, the near-linear rate is optimal up to logarithmic factors over this class. More generally, for datasets generated from an isotropic Gaussian mixture $\mu$ satisfying a mild cost-comparison assumption, uniform sampling yields strong $\varepsilon$-coresets of size $\tilde{O}((k\zeta_\mu+\pi_{\min}^{-1})\varepsilon^{-2})$, where $\pi_{\min}$ is the minimum component weight and $\zeta_\mu$ measures scale imbalance. Our proof uses a base-shift cost decomposition: one query center per component describes the base costs, and graph spanners control the sparse corrections from points switching centers. For general mixtures under cost and tail assumptions, we obtain $\tilde{O}((k\zeta_\mu+\pi_{\min}^{-1})\varepsilon^{-2}\min\{\sqrt{k},\varepsilon^{-2}\})$ samples. We also prove a matching $\tilde{\Omega}(\min\{k^{3/2}\varepsilon^{-2},k\varepsilon^{-4}\})$ lower bound for population approximation by uniform sampling from anisotropic Gaussian mixtures, even with equal weights and a shared covariance matrix. [1] Junqiu Hu, Lingxiao Huang, Jian Li, and Baoduo Xu. Tight coreset bounds for $(k, z)$-clustering in Euclidean and doubling metrics, 2026. arXiv:2610.34373 .

### [690] [Improved Approximation for Weighted $k$-Set Packing via a Simple Two-Phase Approach](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20724)
*Mehrshad Taziki,Rico Zenklusen*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Weighted $k$-set packing asks for a maximum-weight collection of pairwise disjoint sets, each of cardinality at most $k$. For every fixed $k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq1}$, we give a polynomial-time algorithm with approximation factor $\left(1- 1/{\sqrt3} \right)k+O(\log k) \approx 0.4226k + O(\log k)$, improving the previous best factor of $0.4621k + O(\sqrt{k})$ through a simple two-phase approach. In a first phase, our algorithm constructs a packing by processing random weight buckets of varying widths with an unweighted packing algorithm. We show that a small expected weight of this packing relative to the optimum forces a large expected total surplus in the optimum. Surplus quantifies the potential for improving a packing through star swaps. In the second phase, we solve and round a configuration LP to turn sufficiently large surplus into an increase in expected weight. Our procedure can easily be derandomized.

### [691] [Speed-Robust Scheduling for Total Completion Time](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20795)
*Moritz Buchem,Nicole Megow,Morten Weber*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We study two-stage speed-robust scheduling for minimizing total completion time. Jobs must be partitioned into $M$ bags before an adversary reveals the speeds of at most $M$ machines. Each bag is then assigned to one available machine, and the jobs on each machine may be processed in any order independent of the bags. We compare with an optimal schedule that knows the speeds in advance and assigns jobs individually. This model has been studied for makespan minimization. We initiate its study for total completion time, as suggested by Stein and Zhong (TALG 2020). For an unknown number of identical machines, we show that the optimal deterministic robustness factor is exactly~$13/12$, both for unit-size jobs and for arbitrary processing times. For infinitesimally small jobs, the factor lies between $31/30\approx1.0333$ and $28/27\approx1.0370$, well below the optimal makespan factor of about $1.2071$. General speeds make the problem strictly harder: no deterministic algorithm is better than $1.2669$-robust, already for infinitesimally small jobs. We give a $25/16$-robust algorithm for arbitrary processing times and improve the guarantee to $1681/1152\approx1.4592$ for infinitesimally small jobs. Our main tools are a layer decomposition that extends guarantees from unit-size jobs to arbitrary processing times when one assignment satisfies them for every prefix in non-increasing processing-time order, and a threshold analysis of the bag counts produced by greedy assignment rules.

### [692] [Copying along Arithmetic Progressions Cannot Simulate Interleaving with Polylogarithmic Loss](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20980)
*Matthias G. Mayer*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Two classical ways to compress a word are straight-line programs (SLPs), which build it by concatenating smaller pieces, and the Lempel-Ziv 77 (LZ77) factorisation, which copies earlier parts of it; their sizes are measures of repetitiveness. LZ77 approximates the smallest SLP efficiently: it has no more factors than a smallest SLP has size, and yields an SLP at most a logarithmic factor larger in near-linear time. Motivated by online prediction, Kosoy introduced zipline programs, which are analogous to SLPs but interleave their pieces round-robin instead of concatenating them. Her generalisation of LZ77, the arithmetic repetition system, describes a word by copies from one arithmetic progression of positions to a later one. Do arithmetic repetition systems approximate the smallest zipline program as well? Kosoy proved that the least size $\mathrm{ARC}(x)$ of an arithmetic repetition system for a word $x$ of length $n$ is at most a factor $O(n^{1/3})$ larger than the least size $\mathrm{ZLC}(x)$ of a zipline program for it, and asked whether this factor is tight. Her polynomial-time next-letter predictor makes $O(\mathrm{ARC}(x)\log n)$ mistakes, so a polylogarithmic factor would bound its mistakes by $\mathrm{ZLC}(x)\,\mathrm{polylog}(n)$, which no known polynomial-time predictor achieves. We show that the optimal exponent is $1/4$, not $1/3$: $\mathrm{ARC}(x) \le 2n^{1/4}\,\mathrm{ZLC}(x)$ for every word $x$, and at every large enough length $n$ some binary word has $\mathrm{ARC}(x) \ge n^{1/4-o(1)}\,\mathrm{ZLC}(x)$.

### [693] [Subexponential algorithms for structural parameterizations of Vertex Cover in geometric graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21078)
*Marin Bougeret,Juan Pablo Bravo,Daniel Gonçalves*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: A number of recent works have investigated the existence of parameterized subexponential algorithms in geometric graph classes for hitting a fixed small graph as a subgraph or as a minor. In this setting, given an $n$-vertex graph, the goal is to decide in time $n^{O(1)}2^{o(k)}$ if a solution of size at most $k$ exists. Inspired by recent results in kernelization for structural parameters, we investigate subexponential algorithms for the Vertex Cover (VC) problem, but parameterized by distance-to-triviality instead of solution size. More formally, given a fixed "trivial" graph class $\mathcal{C}$, the problem takes as input $(G,X,k)$, where $G \setminus X \in \mathcal{C}$, and asks if $G$ admits a vertex cover of size at most $k$. Our goal is to design algorithms for this problem running in time $n^{O(1)}2^{o(|X|)}$. The motivation is that, since $|X|$ is typically arbitrarily smaller than $k$, such algorithms might be faster than ETH-tight subexponential algorithms parameterized by $k$. We identify two sets of sufficient conditions under which the problem admits a subexponential algorithm: one for the case where $\mathcal{C}$ is the class of paths, and another for the case where $\mathcal{C}$ is the class of graphs of constant treedepth. We also provide two applications of these algorithmic results: we prove that $s$-string graphs and pseudo-disk graphs satisfy the first set of conditions, whereas string graphs satisfy the second set. The two sets share a common condition that might be of independent interest, as it implies a property that bounds the treewidth of any string graph in terms of a given modulator to a fixed graph class $\mathcal{C}$. Finally, concerning more restricted graph classes having the $ASQGM(\omega)$ property (such as map graphs and $H$-minor free graphs), we prove a dichotomy, depending on the maximum treewidth in $\mathcal{C}$.

### [694] [Path-constrained Packing on Trees](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21120)
*Samuel Fiorini,Raoul Luqué,Philipp Pabst,Britta Peis*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: An instance of Budgeted Path-constrained Packing on Trees (BPPT) consists of a graph $G$ together with a spanning tree $T$, a weight $w_e \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ for each tree edge $e \in E(T)$ and a budget $b_f \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}$ for each non-tree edge $f \in E(G) \setminus E(T)$. The goal is to find a maximum weight packing of fundamental cuts respecting the budgets. Equivalently, an instance of BPPT is an integer program of the form $\max \{w^\intercal x : Ax \le b,\ x \in \{0,1\}^n\}$ where $A \in \{0,1\}^{m \times n}$ is a transposed edge-path-tree matrix, $w \in \mathbb{Z}^n_{\ge 0}$ and $b \in \mathbb{Z}^m_{\ge 1}$. We define the congestion $C$ of a BPPT instance as the maximum number of non-zeros in a column of $A$. The unit congestion $UC$ is defined similarly, except that rows with $b_i \ge 2$ are ignored. We also consider the minimum budget $\beta := \min \{b_i : i = 1, \ldots, m\}$. In this paper, we begin the study of BPPT through the lens of the three parameters $C$, $UC$ and $\beta$, and relative to the standard LP relaxation $\max \{w^\intercal x : Ax \le b,\ x \in [0,1]^n\}$. BPPT generalizes the independent set problem in graphs of maximum degree at most $C$ and is a special case of the $b$-matching problem in hypergraphs of rank at most $C$. We obtain approximation algorithms for BPPT with factors $2+UC/2$, $1+C/2$ and $\beta/(\beta-1)$ for $\beta \geq 2$. These bounds are relative to the standard LP relaxation and, as we show, integrality gap tight with respect to parameters $UC$ and $\beta$, and almost integrality gap tight relative to $C$. We complement these results with a $\lceil (C+1)/3 \rceil$-approximation for fixed $C$ which is not relative to the standard LP relaxation and has $\textsf{XP}$ running time parameterized by $C$.

### [695] [An Optimal Online Algorithm for Single-machine Scheduling with Two Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21184)
*Peihai Liu,Kejun Zhao,Xiwen Lu*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: This paper addresses the online two-agent scheduling problem on a single machine, where jobs arrive over time. The objective is to minimize the weighted sum of the agents' makespans, denoted as $C_{\max}^A + \theta C_{\max}^B$, for a given priority weight $\theta \ge 1$. A significant gap has persisted between the established theoretical lower bound on the competitive ratio and the performance of the best-known online algorithms. For the parameter range $1 \leq \theta \leq \tfrac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$, we propose novel online algorithm which achieves a competitive ratio of $1+\tfrac{\theta}{1+\theta}$. This result matches the theoretical lower bound.

### [696] [A Polynomial Time Algorithm for Finding a Minimum 5-Partition of a Submodular Function](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21187)
*Yuhao Liu,Ke Shi,Chao Xu*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: Given a real-valued submodular function on a finite ground set, the minimum $k$-partition problem asks for a partition into $k$ nonempty parts minimizing the sum of their function values. We give a polynomial-time algorithm for $k=5$. The idea follows directly from the previous $k=4$ result, where there is precisely one obstruction for generalizing it to $k=5$. We show the special case can be handled by reasoning about a restricted family of $3$-partitions.

### [697] [Constant-Factor Matching-Size Estimation in Random-Order Streams](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21294)
*Alireza Farhadi,Mohammad Hajiaghayi,Morteza Monemizadeh*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: We give a one-pass algorithm that estimates the maximum matching size of an arbitrary simple graph within a constant factor using $O(\log^2 n)$ bits of space. The edges arrive exactly once in uniformly random order. The algorithm succeeds with probability at least $2/3$, does not require the number of edges in advance, and has worst-case total running time $O((m+1)\log(n+2))$ on a word RAM. Kapralov, Khanna, and Sudan (SODA 2014) obtained a polylogarithmic approximation in polylogarithmic space. Kapralov, Mitrović, Norouzi-Fard, and Tardos (SODA 2020) subsequently gave a constant-factor approximation from independent uniform edge samples and an $O(\log^2 n)$-approximation in random order. We obtain a constant factor in the latter model with the same $O(\log^2 n)$ space bound. The main ingredient is a comparison between the memory states of a recursive sampling algorithm under sampling with and without replacement. We account jointly for the sampled edges retained by the recursion and the positions at which they arrived. Randomized thresholds limit the additional information stored in numerical counters. A bound on the expected work of the entire recursion then removes the loss from its logarithmic depth. The resulting estimator repeatedly improves a coarse estimate while storing only one recursion stack.

### [698] [Reducing Asymmetric Path TSP to Asymmetric TSP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21453)
*Hong Li*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: In the Asymmetric Traveling Salesman Problem (Asymmetric TSP), we are given distances between $n$ vertices that satisfy the triangle inequality but need not be symmetric, and we seek a shortest tour through all vertices. In its path version, Asymmetric Path TSP, two vertices $s$ and $t$ are prescribed, and we seek a shortest path from $s$ to $t$ through all vertices. Both problems are equivalent to their versions with arbitrary nonnegative edge costs on a directed graph, in which vertices may be visited more than once. We show that for all constants $\alpha\ge1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, any $\alpha$-approximation algorithm for Asymmetric TSP yields an $(\alpha+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm for Asymmetric Path TSP. The best previous reduction of this kind, due to Feige and Singh, yields an $\alpha(2+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm. Our result answers an open question of Traub and Vygen. Consequently, every constant-factor approximation guarantee for Asymmetric TSP carries over to Asymmetric Path TSP up to an arbitrarily small additive error.

Abstract: In the Asymmetric Traveling Salesman Problem (Asymmetric TSP), we are given distances between $n$ vertices that satisfy the triangle inequality but need not be symmetric, and we seek a shortest tour through all vertices. In its path version, Asymmetric Path TSP, two vertices $s$ and $t$ are prescribed, and we seek a shortest path from $s$ to $t$ through all vertices. Both problems are equivalent to their versions with arbitrary nonnegative edge costs on a directed graph, in which vertices may be visited more than once. We show that for all constants $\alpha\ge1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, any $\alpha$-approximation algorithm for Asymmetric TSP yields an $(\alpha+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm for Asymmetric Path TSP. The best previous reduction of this kind, due to Feige and Singh, yields an $\alpha(2+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm. Our result answers an open question of Traub and Vygen. Consequently, every constant-factor approximation guarantee for Asymmetric TSP carries over to Asymmetric Path TSP up to an arbitrarily small additive error.

</details>
